officialTimetableIdentity.finding: INM directly identifies its El Borma timetable under Tataouine. Its published coordinates are supporting source context only; the existing app anchor stays unchanged.

primaryEvidence.supports: The operator explicitly describes a residential camp with sports facilities and a medical centre at its El Borma base. Inhabited worker locality is supported; a general civilian town and exact point or residential footprint are not certified.

The operator locates its El Borma oil/gas production field in southwestern Tunisia near the Tunisian-Algerian border. This is the Tunisian industrial locality, not proof about the Algerian namesake municipality.

primaryImages.visualReview: Both full original images personally viewed. The camp image labels Camp Résidentiel and a red closed outline, with no geographic grid/control. The concession image separately marks a national border, names Carthage UTM32N, and depicts a much broader industrial concession. These are different scopes, neither is imported or geometrically fitted.
primaryImages.use: Supporting the distinction between residential camp, field and larger named locality; not proof that both stored anchors are inside the camp.

rootImageReview: Root personally viewed both complete original SITEP images. The camp image illustrates a residential compound; the other image illustrates a much larger concession and border. These distinct scopes are not equivalent and neither is imported as a polygon.

phoneObservationsReviewed.rootVisualConclusion: Unnamed pin among SITEP roads and buildings. The nearby-place address says Al Borma, Algeria; this wording identifies a nearby namesake and does not establish the country at the pin or a surveyed border. It is not a selected locality card.

phoneObservationsReviewed.query: SITEP El Borma camp résidentiel, Tunisie
phoneObservationsReviewed.rootVisualConclusion: Result list contains Camp Résidentiel SITEP El Borma and TPIC Camp of El Borma - Remada. The residential camp is a named public result; no exact footprint is inferred.

Selected public Camp Résidentiel SITEP El Borma card, categorized as a hotel, with visible compound photographs and short plus code M6P9+X7G in the UI record. Supports residential-site identity, not an authoritative polygon or equality of both stored anchors with its footprint.

decision: Support combining the two broad El Borma manual locality choices. The source village identity has continuity from the original western point near the stored reference to the present eastern point; SITEP confirms habitation and INM identifies the Tunisian timetable. Both entries represent the named worker locality context. This does not equate a concession, residential camp, civilian municipality or administrative delegation.
holdResolution: The prior hold requested independent narrower locality/reference scope and a valid proof contract. Authentic node history, direct INM identity, primary operator habitation, and the independently checked existing extension now support the broad named-locality display association. Exact shared residential-camp footprint is not the asserted identity.
qualification: Source-stage review and exact generated-data checks remain required. No coordinate correction, sector merge, new boundary, name change, or country-boundary certification is approved by this display scope decision.
